decision: Retain production provisionally; prioritize coupled-state thermochemistry over selecting NASA from the smaller apparent discrepancy.

primary.inspection: Full seven-page paper read through primary institutional copy; Table I and sections III-V inspected.
primary.findings: Spin-orbit mixing produces an X Omega=1/2 state and two low excited Omega states; a single unmixed Sigma/Pi label is inadequate. Reported D0=66 +/-1 kcal/mol is a theoretical estimate, with neutral O asymptote fine structure explicitly neglected in the energetics discussion.

primary.inspection: Publisher abstract only; full article and supporting numerical tables unavailable in this review.
primary.findings: Calculated neutral KO hf298=55.9 kJ/mol; spin-free Sigma state lower than Pi by 1.1 kJ/mol at 0 K. These are not a complete spin-orbit thermal function.

limitations: Do not treat Te gaps as rovibronic origins or construct an unqualified three-level correction; rotation, vibration and state mixing differ.
Lee 2002 explicitly requires multireference treatment of the long-range neutral dissociation region; its printed O fine-structure ordering is not used as an atomic reference.
JANAF 1967-era thermochemistry and Gurvich 1982 original source pages were not independently reaudited.
followups: Acquire DOI 10.1021/jp9034826 full text and supporting Tables S1/S3/S6 to reconcile hf298, spin-orbit convention and neutral-atom asymptotes.
Build and validate derivative-consistent coupled-state thermal functions before a modern energy-plus-thermal candidate and finite substitution.
The missing follow-up source is not a merge gate for the scoped retain-and-record source audit.
